chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when traveling or when a need hastened him, would combine the Dhuhr and Asr prayers, and the Maghrib and the last Isha prayer. He said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no harm in hastening the last Isha prayer during travel before the twilight disappears.'

key_terms.اَلشَّفَقُ: Twilight (specifically the red glow after sunset used for time calculation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on combining and hastening prayers during travel in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* highlights the Prophetic precedent for *jam' taqdim* (early combination) of prayers during travel or necessity, a foundational concept in Shia fiqh for easing religious obligations under hardship. The Imam’s specific clarification regarding performing Isha before the disappearance of twilight (*shafaq*) underscores the flexibility in defining prayer times when circumstances demand urgency, distinguishing it from mere delay. This ruling reflects the Shia emphasis on practicality and the removal of hardship (*raf' al-haraj*) in worship.
